best_for: Home Windows users who want a tiny, fast image viewer and batch converter, and small offices willing to pay a modest one-time license for it.

points.title: Free at home, paid at work
points.text: IrfanView is free for private, non-commercial use, and also for schools, universities, museums, libraries and charities. Businesses must buy a license.

points.title: A perpetual business license
points.text: A single commercial license is listed at US$18.00 or EUR 15.00, perpetual and valid for both 32-bit and 64-bit versions, with discounts from 11 licenses. The site asks companies to email for quotes. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Small and quick
points.text: The download is about 8 MB. Beyond viewing, it converts, batch-processes, scans, prints and runs slideshows.

points.title: Some formats need plugins
points.text: The base install covers common formats. Rarer formats and PDF support need the separate plugins pack, and PDF also needs Ghostscript of the same bitness as IrfanView. The Microsoft Store version cannot take plugins.

points.title: Old Windows still works
points.text: It runs on Windows XP through 11. This page lists 32-bit and 64-bit installers that install for all users; the publisher also makes an Arm64 build that is not listed here. The listing keeps 3 versions.

points.title: No Mac or Linux version
points.text: There is no native build for either. The FAQ suggests Wine on Linux or a Wine wrapper on Mac, using the ZIP version.

points.title: Portable by design
points.text: Every version runs portable. Copy the program folder to a USB stick or unzip the ZIP there.
